sections.label: Face
sections.text:
Itching, burning, and crusts on right zygoma.
Lupus, caries ; open, bleeding cancer. Tip of nose
painful.

sections.label: Mouth
Ears
sections.text:
Watery discharge; also fetid pus. Tetter on
and around ears, extending to external meatus.

sections.label: Throat
sections.text:
Spongy feeling; very dry and cold air pass-
ing over parts causes pain. Breath, tongue, and throat
fel cold. Uvula and tonsils swollen. A small, dry spot
in throat ; must sip water frequently. Hawking of
mucus. Swelling and suppuration of glands of throat.
Head drawn to one side by swellings in neck. Sore
throat from inhaling the least cold air. Heat and itch-
ing in throat.

sections.label: Stomach
sections.text:
Cool feeling in stomach before and after
eating. Cool feeling in whole abdomen. Desire for
cheese.

sections.label: Stool
sections.text:
Diarrhoea from coffee and fruit, thin, yellow,
urgent; worse in morning.

sections.label: Chest
sections.text:
Coldness in chest. The neck is studded
with tumors. Induration of mammae. Haemorrhage
from lungs.


247

sections.label: Extremities
sections.text:
Sprained pain in wrist. Tips of
fingers sensitive to cold. Tetter on hands. Cold feet.
Syphilitic ulcers on lower limbs, with hard swelling
around. White swelling.

sections.label: Sleep
sections.text: Cannot sleep from coldness in throat.

sections.label: Female
sections.text:
Induration and inflammation of mammae.
Sensitive to cold air. Bad smelling leucorrhoea.

sections.label: Respiratory
sections.text:
Asthmatic after lying down (trachea
feels narrow), preceded by formication.

sections.label: Skin
Modalities
sections.text:
Worse, slightest exposure to cold air.
Better after eating.

221 CITRUS LIMONUM.

CITRUS LIMONUM.

Lemon. Rutacese.

A popular remedy with the Arabians.

"The Citrus Medica, like the orange tree, is a native of Asia. It was intro-
duced into Europe from Persia or Media, was first cultivated in Greece, afterwards
in Italy, so early as the second century. It is considered almost a specific for
prevention and cure of scurvy. Kevillont, a French physician, recommends it as
a gargle in diphtheritic affection of fauces, but states that it is without action on
the white lenticular patches." — U. S. D.

Clinical Authorities. — Diphtheria, recommended by Buchner ; Dysentery,
natives of Tchian, Persia, Ausland, p. 18, 1855; Dropsy and hydrothorax, Schwabe,
Casper's Wschrft., 1843, No. 8 ; Dropsy after scarlatina, Biittner, Pr. Med. Ztg., 1842,
No. 26; Dropsy with splenitis. Gross, Horn. Arch., v. 20, p. 178; Hydrothorax (two
cases), Borner, Frank's Mag., v. 1, p. 1 ; Hydrothorax and general anasarca, Frank's
Mag., V. 1, p. 157 ; Convulsions, caused by eating the seeds of Datura Stramonium,
Euckert's Horn. Therap., p. 377; Cancer, Denny, B. J. H., v. 24, p. 518; Willis
and Brondini ; Sunstroke, Med. Inves., v. 8, p. 477.
